Sasha: Quick question — for the /v1/generate endpoint: if we set a platform-level default model pin, does an older client that sends an explicit model param still get the explicit model? cc @Marta

Marta: Explicit model param currently wins. Default pinning only applies when the client does not specify a model. That said, there's a legacy exception in the routing layer for clients sending header `X-Client-Version: <1.5.0>` — they are routed to the legacy-compat pool.

Kevin: That legacy exception is the source of confusion. Two gotchas: 1) legacy pool may have different quantization/profile, 2) fallback behavior differs (no auto-upgrade to pins).

Sasha: Ah, we hit that in a couple of support tickets. Is the header-based exception documented anywhere?

Marta: Not clearly. We added a short note in the internal rollout doc but not on the public API page. Right now the decision tree is roughly:

```
if client sends model param -> serve requested model
else if client sends X-Client-Version < 1.5.0 -> route to legacy-compat pool
else -> apply platform default pin
```

Lin: Can we consider changing to a feature-gate header instead of version parsing? e.g., `X-Compat-Mode: legacy` so clients that want the old behavior can opt in explicitly. Safer than inferring from version.

Marta: I like that. Proposed plan: add `X-Compat-Mode` for explicit opt-in, keep version inference for 3 months as migration, then remove inference. Need comms + deprecation window.

Kevin: For rollout, also verify response shapes. Legacy pool returns `generation.metadata.model_revision` as string; new pools use `generation.model.revision` nested object. We should add a compatibility shim for the top-level string field for 3 months.

Sasha: Sounds good. Concrete asks: can eng-platform add the header gate + router change? Can docs team publish a deprecation note? Can runtime add shim for the string field?

Marta: Eng-platform work: add header accept/override and toggle behind feature flag. ETA: 1 week for small change + tests. Docs: I'll draft a short deprecation notice and a migration guide (how to set header, example SDK patch). Runtime: I'll open a runtime PR for the shim; need review from Kevin.

Kevin: I'll review runtime PR. Also please include an automated smoke test that calls /v1/generate with older shape to ensure shim keeps returning legacy field.

deploy-bot: deploy queued to canary (eng-platform/router) — job id: canary-2321.

Lin: Timeline suggestion: publish docs + SDK snippets on day 0, enable header gate in canary on day 3, flip inference-migration off (stop inferring from version) on day 90. That's a 3-month runway.

Sasha: +1. Also add an internal note for Support so they know to ask customers to set `X-Compat-Mode: legacy` if they need old behavior.

Marta: I'll add a short Support playbook and a sample curl snippet:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "X-Compat-Mode: legacy" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Sasha: Thanks. Can we also include a policy: default pin changes (breaking) must have 90d deprecation + automated compat tests before rollout?

Kevin: Agree. Add that to the rollout checklist.

Marta: I'll drop a PR to the eng-platform runbook with: header gate + shim + 90d deprecation policy + support playbook. Tagging this thread for follow-ups. :raised_hands:

Sasha: Perfect — thanks all.
